problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 7\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}},$ where ${c}_{1}=-{b}_{3}$, ${c}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}{b}_{1}$ and ${c}_{3}=2{b}_{2}?$

feedback.problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}},$ where ${c}_{1}=-{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{2}-{b}_{1}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=-{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{2}-{b}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the first equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{2}=-{c}_{1}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{2}=-{c}_{1}-{b}_{1}\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=-{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3{b}_{1}+5{b}_{2} \\  & =3(-{c}_{1}-{c}_{2})+5(-{c}_{1}) \\  & =-3{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2}-5{c}_{1} \\  & =-8{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$
